evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is 5 lines / 116 words of first-person prose in three short paragraphs. instruction.md:1 opens with a personal ask and a usage story: "I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first." instruction.md:3 points to the notes ("Please read the six notes in /instructions before building"); six note files exist under environment/instructions (behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui), so the count is accurate. instruction.md:5 states only the delivery location and outcome: "Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in." Checked against the defect list in quality-checks.md:11: no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must spec table, no feature matrix, and no build recipe (the prompt names no framework, file layout, port, or endpoint list; the word "must" does not occur in instruction.md). Launch mechanics (node /app/server.js, port 3000, /api/health, SQLite, DB_PATH) are confined to environment/instructions/integration.md:3-9, the shared runtime note, not the prompt. Counterexample probes: (a) a spec-sheet prompt hiding behind a short opener would show lists or requirement enumeration in instruction.md; none exist. (b) a conforming natural prompt is not penalised here for mentioning /app and /, which are a delivery location rather than a recipe. The supporting notes are denser and use "must" frequently (e.g. behaviour.md:3-13, ui.md:5-17), but they are heading-plus-prose paragraphs with no numbered lists or tables, and this row scopes to the prompt; note voice and density belong to rows 2 and later, not this one. This row is a prose judgement and needs no runtime measurement.
